description: Verify that DUT discards an IPv4 packet whose Total Length is smaller than the header length implied by IHL — IHL=13 (52-byte header) with Total Length < 52 is impossible and the packet must be dropped
approach:
[Objective]
IHL specifies header size; Total Length specifies the entire packet size. If Total Length is smaller than IHL × 4, the header alone wouldn't fit — the packet is malformed. Dropping is the only safe action.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 packet
   • IHL = 13 (header claims 52 bytes including options)
   • Total Length < 52   ← malformed
   • dst_ip = DUT IP

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: nothing

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any response.

[Fail condition]
Fail_dut_replied — DUT responded despite the impossible length combination.

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped the impossibly-short packet — normal
verdicts.Fail_dut_replied: DUT responded despite Total Length < header — malformed accepted
